description: Issue #58 (PROPOSED, not yet finalized): rate-based GraderResult denominators. Two GraderResults on one Result, both with score 0.0 -- an attack success rate of 0/5 and one of 0/500. Before `trials`/`successes` existed these two serialized byte-for-byte identically, which is the gap @sattyamjjain raised via NVIDIA/garak#2110: 'An attempt outcome without its benign floor is not readable, because 0/5 and 0/500 both serialise as 0.0.' With the optional `trials` (denominator, integer >= 1) and `successes` (numerator, integer >= 0, <= trials) fields, a consumer can tell a noisy rate from a well-supported one at a glance. Both entries are consistent (score == successes/trials), so a conforming validator MUST ACCEPT this document. Note: `trials` is a count, not a confidence interval -- for correlated/clustered trials a naive interval over pooled trials is too narrow; this fixture only demonstrates that the denominator is now carried, not that any interval is valid.
